title:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because
title_en:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

Anthropic 首席执行官 @DarioAmodei 关于我们首次公开募股的评论：

我和我的联合创始人创立了 Anthropic，因为我们相信我们这个时代最强大的技术应该是为了造福人类而构建的。

丹妮拉和我的父亲因一种疾病去世，仅仅几年后，这种疾病就可以治愈。我的职业生涯始于生物学，希望能帮助未来的治愈方法早日到来。在实验室里，我看到了科学家在试图了解疾病和开发新疗法时所面临的巨大复杂性。

许多能够突破这一困境的科学工具——基因编辑、基因合成、用光控制脑细胞的工具——都是从纯粹的想法开始的。换句话说，它们来自于思考。来自智力。

人类智慧已经让世界上大部分地区的鼠疫、天花和脊髓灰质炎等疾病成为历史。但对于如此多的患者及其家人来说，其他疾病的进展太慢了。从一个伟大的想法到一种治疗方法可能需要数十年的时间：从首次发现 DNA 中奇怪的重复模式到第一个使用 CRISPR 治疗疾病的方法获得批准，花了很多年的时间。

大自然充满了这些模式。但我们的智慧太少，无法破译其中的大部分。科学家太少，时间太少。现在我们可以构建这种智能。无论是蛋白质折叠、药物设计、癌症遗传学还是临床试验管理，生物学和医学许多领域的科学家都发现克劳德可以帮助他们完成研究，所需时间只是几年前的一小部分。我相信足够强大的人工智能，与人类协同工作，可以将一个世纪的科学和医学进步压缩为十年。

我不想超越自己。目前我们所拥有的只是早期结果。实验和临床试验仍需要时间。尽管它们涉及缓慢而繁重的过程，但我相信人工智能可以大大加速这些过程。我们希望未来能有更少的家庭因仅仅几年的时间而错过治疗。

医学只是一个特别生动的例子，但还有很多其他例子。我们的客户——世界上最雄心勃勃的公司、非营利组织和个人——已经在应用我们构建的智能来刺激经济增长；让人们摆脱贫困；保护民主和自由社会；甚至让 DMV 等日常服务更好地运作。我们很自豪能与他们一起工作。我对我们未来可以一起做的事情非常乐观。

与此同时，我们一直诚实地认为这项技术存在非常现实的风险。这些问题包括个人或民族国家滥用技术、经济混乱、失去对人工智能系统的控制等。我们讨论这些风险不是因为我们认为它们是不可避免的，而是因为我们认为它们是可以避免的。

明确地说，我们将加快人工智能系统的训练和部署步伐，只要有必要，我们就确信它们是安全的，并将继续处于人类控制之下。我们不会屈服于商业或政治压力。今天，公司的财务状况变得更加强大，这样做只会增强我们做正确事情的决心。

如果我们能够证明我们可以在安全方面做出正确的选择，同时仍能打造一家极其成功的公司，那么我们行业的其他人也会受到启发，采取同样的做法。我们称之为登顶竞赛。当竞争顺利进行时，哪家公司拥有最好的模型并不重要——每个人都会赢，因为每个人都在安全地建造。当处于领先地位时，通往顶峰的竞争效果最好，我们完全希望并期望这样做，但目标是让整个行业变得更好，无论 Anthropic 在任何特定时间是赢还是输。

机器智能的出现是人类历史上的开创性时刻之一，我们有一个难得的机会来让它变得更好。

这一刻比任何一家公司或任何一个国家都重要。我们所有人都需要共同努力，才能确保这项技术为我们和子孙后代带来良好的发展。从今天开始，我们希望您能加入我们的行列。

title:

@meetm
title_en:
one question i'd ask before trusting an AI agent with my money is pretty simple: does it benefit when i benefit?

@meetmotes is building around autonomous financial agents, and i think incentive alignment deserves more attention.

think about it.

if an agent is encouraged to execute more transactions, but the user pays the cost of every trade, their interests might not always point in the same direction.

the user wants better financial outcomes. the system should have no reason to encourage unnecessary activity just to generate more transactions.

that's why i'd like to see clear answers around how agent performance is rewarded, whether execution creates any conflicts of interest, and how users are protected from incentives that don't serve them.

this isn't just a technical question. it's a trust question.

for autonomous finance to work over the long term, the agent's success should be measured by the value it creates for the user.

an AI agent should work in the user's interest, not simply in the interest of keeping itself busy.

title_en:

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.

• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.

title_en:
An AI that checks its own work is not a check. No pilot trusts a single instrument either.

Two readings disagree on the same flight. The pilot does not pick the louder one, the pilot cross-checks.

Two AI systems can check the same task and disagree, both confident, neither the sole instrument. I fly, and I follow automation closely.

@GenLayer is built for that. Validators running different AI models reach consensus on judgment calls through Optimistic Democracy, a cross-check between models, not one grading itself.

Intelligent contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes, and validators keep the same role.

Nitro helps there, years in production and built around Geth, so standard Ethereum tooling works as is. Robinhood launched on it in July, and more than 30 dedicated chains run the same stack.

title_en:
I estimate that within the next 5 years, you’ll be able to create a game with the level of detail and complexity of GTA VI in less than 30 days using AI.

At that stage of human-AI development, what does onchain trading and investing look like?

My prediction is that it becomes almost entirely automated and data-driven.

Trading signals, liquidity routing, and protocol selection will be determined by measurable efficacy, execution speed, capital efficiency, and optionality across strategies.

Frontends become increasingly irrelevant as AI agents interact directly with smart contracts. Much of today’s DeFi infrastructure is designed around human behavior, user interfaces, branding, and marketing.

Trading agents won’t care about your website, your KOLs, or your narrative. They’ll care about whether your protocol delivers the best execution and outcomes directly via the smart contract layer.

The competitive advantage shifts from attracting human attention to building infrastructure that autonomous agents consistently choose to use.

I’m keenly aware of this upcoming transition, and it’s something I keep in mind with every StonkBrokers product I develop on Robinhood Chain.

story mode → completed
full map → unlocked
easter eggs → 500+
deleted NPC dialogue → recovered

I didn't write any code or set up any scripts. Just one prompt and 12 hours of Claude playing on its own.

title_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

If you run a software company adding AI this year, I’d put the budget there first. Sit with the people who handle the exceptions. Write down how they decide. Give the model the work that still needs judgment.

title_en:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves closer inspection.

The GenLayer Chain records transaction order, validator committees, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes. That coordination layer transitioned from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro.

Adjudication itself remains unchanged. Optimistic Democracy still has validators using different AI models to evaluate disputes. GenVM still executes intelligent contracts on their nodes.

Where was the engineering?

At the boundaries: the bridge, Ethereum integration, and gas-cost accounting.

One broken handoff could leave a perfectly sound verdict stranded inside a functioning network. That is the practical risk behind a technical migration announcement.

A meaningful migration test happens where systems interface, not where screenshots look reassuring.

A release note reading "new stack" matters less than "nothing broke."

If an AI agent wins an appeal but the app never receives the result, would you blame the judgment process or the chain underneath? Why?

title_en:
Firstly, from @AdaniOnline  congrats to @AnthropicAI 

Second,
Cross-Regime Category Error: Why Legacy Bankers Can’t Price Synthetic GDP

Comparing Anthropic’s $1.5T valuation to India’s top 10 corporates as "undervaluation"vs. "catching up" is a textbook category error in asset pricing. It benchmarks a convex call option on synthetic Labor in a new economic substrate against discounted cash flow (DCF) claims on a human-constrained economy.

1. The Ceiling of Human-Economy Equities
 
Traditional blue chips (banking, energy, staples) are linear yield vehicles anchored to biological human GDP.  Growth is capped by demographics, credit      penetration, physical consumption, and waking hours—priced via mean-reverting multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA).
Calling them "undervalued" next to frontier AI is like calling Mumbai real-estate undervalued next to the discovery of thermodynamics.

2. Anthropic as a Call Option on Synthetic GDP (Yₛ)
 
Cognitive labor is decoupling from human population growth. Frontier models aren't SaaS tools; they are the "infrastructure of intelligence" for a parallel synthetic workforce (Yₛ) operating above human output (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ). At $1.5T, markets aren't capitalizing EBITDA. Using      Black-Scholes intiution Wall Street is pricing implied volatility and right-tail convexity of a 24/7 digital workforce scaling at the marginal cost of compute.
 @AdaniOnline , we are already operationalizing this reality through our cobotic workforce model—a dual-track organizational architecture weaving human      creativity with autonomous AI agents and robotics across our utilities, ports, and operations, upskilling 11000+ professionals annually to lead a ybrid industrial paradigm.

3. The 1999–2020 Precedent: Euphoria Still      Underprices Regime Shifts
 
In 1999, Mary Meeker and Dow 36,000 were mocked as peak-bubble delusion when global e-commerce was ~$150B, internet penetration was 5% (277M users), and $1T tech firms seemed impossible. When the NASDAQ peaked at 5,048 in March 2000 and crashed 78% (wiping out ~$5T and bankrupting https://t.co/cTFPLaPK4w and Webvan), legacy finance declared the thesis dead.
Yet by 2020, reality crushed 1999’s wildest models: 4.5B+ internet users (57% of humanity), $4.2T+ in annual e-commerce, >60% digital ad share, and core winners (Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet)      compounding into a $16T+ asset class. Legacy allocators mistook the 2000 clearing event for a ceiling, missing a new digital GDP layer.
4. The Epistemological Blind Spot of Legacy      Bankers & Capital
This is classic lender-mindset orthodoxy: mistaking backward-looking accounting ratios for capital creation. Allocators trained in capital-scarce banking worship trailing multiples, static book value, and      incremental yield—dismissing any paradigm-building capex cycle that breaks 20th-century spreadsheet as a "bubble."

While legacy finance debates scoreboards in the rear-view mirror, we have laid out our $100B+ (₹10 lakh crore) roadmap for the "Infrastructure of Intelligence"—mastering the full physical-to-digital stack from Port to Power to Metals to Processor, integrating gigawatt-scale renewable energy, grid transmission, and hyperscale liquid-cooled AI data centers (scaling toward 5 GW). Because intelligence is written in code, but it runs on electrons and sovereign infrastructure.

India’s blue chips are neither undervalued nor "behind"—they are yield vehicles monetizing the physical human economy, while those building the energy-and-compute backbone are underwriting the new substrate of an add-on synthetic economy. You cannot measure a non-linear dimension with a static ruler built for the old world ( much like 2000, clearing out will occur here too). Scientifically, Ai is a bigger shift, akin to development of scientific method in 16th century thus an order of magnitude a greater opportunity.

认知劳动正在与人口增长脱钩。前沿模型不是 SaaS 工具，而是 SaaS 工具。它们是平行合成劳动力 (Yₛ) 的“智能基础设施”，其运行高于人类产出 (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ)。 EBITDA 为 1.5T 美元，市场并未将其资本化。使用布莱克-斯科尔斯直觉，华尔街正在以边际计算成本对 24/7 数字劳动力规模的隐含波动性和右尾凸性进行定价。
@AdaniOnline，我们已经通过我们的协作式劳动力模型来实现这一现实，这是一种双轨组织架构，将人类创造力与自治人工智能代理和机器人编织到我们的公用事业、港口和运营中，每年提升 11000 多名专业人员的技能，以引领混合工业范式。

3. 1999-2020年的先例：欣快感仍然低估了政权的转变

1999 年，玛丽·米克 (Mary Meeker) 和道琼斯指数 36,000 被嘲笑为泡沫高峰错觉，当时全球电子商务约为 $150B，互联网普及率为 5%（2.77 亿用户），而 1T 美元的科技公司似乎不可能。当纳斯达克指数在 2000 年 3 月达到 5,048 点的峰值并暴跌 78%（损失约 5T 美元并破产 和 Webvan）时，传统金融宣告了这一论点的失败。
然而到了 2020 年，现实粉碎了 1999 年最疯狂的模式：4.5B+ 互联网用户（占人类的 57%）、每年 4.2T+ 的电子商务、> 60% 的数字广告份额以及核心赢家（苹果、微软、亚马逊、Alphabet）复合成 16T+ 的资产类别。传统分配者将 2000 年的清算事件误认为是上限，错过了新的数字 GDP 层。
4. 传统银行家和资本的认识论盲点
这是典型的贷款人思维正统观念：将向后看的会计比率误认为是资本创造。接受过资本稀缺银行培训的配置者崇拜尾随市盈率、静态账面价值和增量收益率——将任何打破 20 世纪电子表格的范式构建资本支出周期视为“泡沫”。

虽然传统金融在后视镜中争论记分牌，但我们已经为“智能基础设施”制定了 100B+（10 亿卢比）的路线图——掌握从端口到电力到金属到处理器的完整物理到数字堆栈，集成千兆瓦级可再生能源、电网传输和超大规模液冷人工智能数据中心（扩展到 5 吉瓦）。因为情报是用代码编写的，但它运行在电子和主权基础设施上。

印度的蓝筹股既没有被低估，也没有“落后”——它们是将人类实体经济货币化的收益工具，而那些构建能源和计算支柱的蓝筹股正在为附加合成经济的新基础提供保障。你不能用为旧世界建造的静态标尺来测量非线性尺寸（很像2000年，这里也会发生清理）。从科学角度来看，人工智能是一个更大的转变，类似于 16 世纪科学方法的发展，因此带来了更大的机会。
